row.evidence: Crowdin's pricing page lists "SCIM user provisioning" among the Business plan features of Crowdin Enterprise, and Crowdin's docs say Business and Enterprise plans are bought through the Sales team.
row.notes: Status stays gated, but the June plan name and prices are revised. SCIM and SAML sit on the Business plan of Crowdin Enterprise (plans: Team+, Business, Enterprise). Upgrading to Business or Enterprise goes through Sales, so the price is Contact Sales (c5, c7, c8). The SCIM tie to Business comes from the pricing page's client-side bundle: the Business card's feature list includes businessScimProvisioning (c3). crowdin.com/enterprise also lists 'SAML SSO & SCIM provisioning' (c2). The pricing-page tooltip describes the behaviour: IdP access invites the member, and removing access removes them from the organization (c4). Crowdin publishes no SCIM setup guide, endpoint or attribute list. June's 'Team: $179/mo flat' and 'Enterprise: $450+/mo' are dropped: the plan table renders only in a browser and headless Chrome failed on crowdin.com (ERR_TOO_MANY_RETRIES), so no price could be read. Plans on crowdin.com are Free, Pro, Team, Team+ and Business. SAML SSO creates accounts on first login (JIT). The Enterprise REST API v2 has full user, group and team management.

limitations.text: Crowdin publishes no SCIM setup guide, base URL, token procedure or attribute list. SCIM is known only from the pricing page and the Crowdin Enterprise landing page.

capabilities.notes: Users are invited (POST /users), not created directly. Groups and teams have their own endpoints. Project roles are set through project-member and permission endpoints.

audit_log_api.notes: Organization and per-user security logs (security-log scope).

rate_limits.text: 20 simultaneous API requests per account; 429 when exceeded.

okta.notes: Okta's Crowdin app is marked SWA only (read from page markup, last updated Jul. 10 2015). Crowdin's own guide sets up SAML with a custom Okta app. Whether SCIM works with Okta is not documented.

entra.notes: Crowdin documents SAML with a Microsoft Azure enterprise application. No Crowdin entry exists in the Microsoft Learn SaaS tutorial index.

google.notes: Crowdin documents a Google Workspace SAML app.

onelogin.notes: Crowdin's guide uses OneLogin's generic 'SAML Test (IdP)' connector.

open_questions: No price is captured for any plan: the pricing table renders client-side and crowdin.com blocked headless Chrome. June's $179/mo Team and $450+/mo Enterprise figures are unverified.
SCIM details are undocumented: base URL, token source, SCIM version, supported IdPs, attributes, groups, filtering, pagination and whether SAML must be configured first.
Whether the SCIM-removed member's seat is freed and whether their contributions are kept is not documented.
Which Crowdin Enterprise plans include API access is not stated. The API reference applies to all Crowdin Enterprise organizations without naming a plan.
